chapter: Louisville, Buck and the carnival years
title: Teenage jobs: tobacco hogsheads, shoe shining, restaurant
summary: He describes hauling tobacco and keeping busy at every job to make money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: ... about the bicycle and it didn't cost him nothing' cause I didn't grab it, let it go against me and ever after we did all right.
You were about to talk about the job in the tobacco company.
I was down at tobacco Hodgets --

Tobacco in a Hodgets, in like a keg, that's a Hodgets and you roll this on a flat car, wagon and they put sticks up to keep from rolling off and you drive it to where it's got to go and they take it off.
Now you were pretty young, weren't you?
Yeah, in my early teens, but I was ready, I was ready.
Anything. Wide open, I was ready, ready to go to work anywhere, do anything. Make some money. Money was all the rage then. Needed the money to pay bills and everything. You know?
You were a hard worker then.

Well, it was a hard try anyway. My enthusiasm was at the peak, at its peak. I kept myself busy at all times, trying to get this and that. If I wasn't doing one thing I was doing another. I went to shining shoes, and if I wasn't shining shoes I was hoving bubbles, I hoved butts, I'd sell rags and things back then and coal, I kept myself busy all the time. I used to have to get up in the morning to go to the restaurant to get the fire rolling
